items.title: Disability community surprised by scale of planned NDIS overhaul
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler has defended the government's latest cost-cutting changes to the scheme in an interview with the ABC, amid an avalanche of participant concern.

items.title: Research for Congress raises doubts over AUKUS submarines
items.description: The US Navy's submarine-building program — which Australia is relying on for its naval fleet — risks another slowdown due to delays awarding a critical construction contract.

items.title: Sheraz was treated like an 'infidel' in Afghanistan, now he's being honoured
items.description: Sheraz worked with Australian and US troops in Afghanistan, as a result his family were targeted by the Taliban. This Anzac Day he's being heroed.

items.title: In dying, James Valentine taught us how to live. I'll miss being his sidekick
items.description: Children grew up with him, adults grew old with him, he kept us connected to our city, the world and each other. James helped us make sense of life and gave us permission to laugh at the absurdity of it all — and ourselves.

items.title: Live: Major stock suffers ASX wipe-out
items.description: Major healthcare stock Cochlear crashed yesterday. Buyers have not moved in today. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Actor suing Rebel Wilson agrees bath incident was 'strange and bizarre'
items.description: A young actor suing Rebel Wilson for defamation has given details in court about an incident at Bondi Beach, which she claims the Hollywood star has since mischaracterised.

items.title: Live: Iran attacks three cargo ships in strait, US Navy Secretary departs role
items.description: Iran has said it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the US naval blockade remains in place. Follow live.

items.title: 'If only': Indonesian MP floats toll on key international shipping route
items.description: The suggestion of levying ships using the Malacca Strait was suggested and then walked back by Indonesia's finance minister, but it has prompted a response from Canberra.

items.title: 'Not a nice place to live at the moment': Kununurra residents at wits' end
items.description: Stolen cars and accommodation break-ins have led to growing frustration in Western Australia's north.

items.title: 'We're not ready to leave': Inside the messy dynamic of a no-grounds eviction
items.description: Evicting a tenant without cause offers landlords a simple way out, but the issue can be much more complex than it appears. One such example of that complexity is Eleanor Kahlo's case of her no-grounds eviction.

items.title: Every Glock handgun issued to Qld police to be tested
items.description: The Glock pistol has been identified to have a potential fault that could cause them to fire multiple shots instead of one.

items.title: Authors leave publisher after kids book cancelled for illustrator's comments
items.description: Writers including Evelyn Araluen and Randa Abdel-Fattah have left University of Queensland Press after the publisher axed publication of an Indigenous kids book over its illustrator's past 'anti-Semitic' comments.

items.title: Man accused of threatening to 'blow up' Perth Airport faces court after evacuation
items.description: A man who allegedly threatened to "blow up" Perth Airport's main international terminal, forcing its evacuation and causing traveller chaos, has appeared in court.

items.title: 'Bordering on bullying': Voss hits out at coverage of Hollands
items.description: Michael Voss has called out the media for the way it has covered Elijah Hollands's medical episode, saying the coverage of the 23-year-old "bordered on bullying".

items.title: The 'plunk' sound of rain makes seeds sprout faster, scientists find
items.description: Scientists say they have the first direct evidence that seeds can sense the sound of rain, and will sprout faster when they do.

items.title: Small WA town takes centre stage for Netflix series filming
items.description: There is a buzz about town in a small community north of Perth as filming begins for a new Netflix series.

items.title: Genesis Owusu goes out of his way to connect with fans — and detractors
items.description: Genesis Owusu today releases his new track Life Keeps Going from his upcoming third album Redstar Wu & the Worldwide Scourge, as he encourages engagement with people who don't agree with his political views.

items.title: Removing plastic from our food chain yields quick results, researchers say
items.description: Perth researchers find levels of plastic chemicals in the body can be reduced within a week by avoiding plastic food packaging and kitchen utensils.

items.title: Author of damning report into CFMEU says he did not keep 'trivial' records
items.description: The inquiry has been investigating alleged misconduct and violence within the Queensland branch of the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU).

items.title: A dozen new offences added to LNP's adult crime, adult time laws in Qld
items.description: Conspiring to commit murder, unlawful stalking and riot are among 12 new offences that juveniles can now be sentenced as adults for.

items.title: Kingpin's private phone calls break open Mongols' 'culture of silence'
items.description: Detectives say bikies are recruiting inside Northern Territory prisons, as a kingpin's tapped private phone calls offer a rare glimpse into the underground world of outlaw motorcycle gangs.

items.title: New AI threat looms but Australian firms don't have access needed to prepare
items.description: Local banks, power providers and infrastructure firms do not have access to test their systems against a powerful new AI cybersecurity risk, Anthropic's Mythos, which has not been made public.

items.title: This man plays the last post to a different fallen Anzac every day
items.description: Adam Farquharson feels the honour of Anzac Day every day as he plays to a different veteran's grave.

items.title: Two women on the hunt to find every soldier settler name in El Arish
items.description: Anzac Day holds meaning for every Australian, but for Marie Carman and Lorelei King, it is another reminder of their deeply personal mission to uncover the forgotten stories of the soldiers who helped build their town.

items.title: E-7 Wedgetails are world leading, so why are they up for replacement?
items.description: Australia's fleet of world-leading surveillance aircraft is set to be replaced and analysts say the planes could be replaced by drones.
